newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta quiet after Thursday's demonstration.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta quiet after Thursday's demonstration.

text.p: Jakarta was quiet on Friday after a low-key demonstration on Thursday by about 300 supporters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
"There are no protests planned for Friday. We are waiting for a reaction from the police," said Edi Siswoyo, a member of Megawati's faction ousted from the official Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI)

Money market dealers said Thursday's demonstration had put pressure on the Indonesian rupiah, which was down against the dollar on Friday. At 0659 GMT, it was quoted at 2,359.10/2360 per dollar compared with 2,357.50/.75 on Thursday.
"The rupiah remains under pressure due to sustained overseas rupiah selling after Megawati supporters staged demonstrations in parliament yesterday," one Japanese bank dealer said.
In June the party was taken over and Megawati ousted as leader by a government-backed rival, deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi.
The demonstration was staged to protest against what her backers say is unequal treatment by the authorities following a July 27 attack on PDI headquarters and subsequent riots that rocked Jakarta.

A total of 115 Megawati supporters occupying the PDI building were released in November after serving four months in jail for disobeying police orders. None of the 200 or so Surjadi supporters who attacked the PDI headquarters were arrested.
